evidence_quotes: La Tirana, Chile recorded 3 of the 12 events, including two M6.1 quakes on January 30 and February 2
Three events triggered tsunami alerts: Quakes near the Kermadec Islands (M5.7), New Britain/PNG (M5.5), and Tual, Indonesia (M5.5)
Several events occurred at depths under 10 km — including Tual, Indonesia (5.4 km) and New Britain, PNG (7.4 km)
Chile's northern region warrants continued monitoring: Three events in roughly three weeks near La Tirana
Indonesia and the Western Pacific remain high-alert zones
criticisms: No concrete 24-hour actions are specified — the report never tells a coordinator to 'alert county X', 'request USGS update on Y', 'verify shelter capacity in Z', or any equivalent executable step.

Monitoring priorities are vague: 'review preparedness plans' and 'continued monitoring' are not specific watch items — no magnitude thresholds, no specific fault systems, no named agencies to contact.

The tsunami-flagged events (Kermadec Islands, New Britain/PNG, Tual) are described but no follow-up action is recommended — e.g., whether tsunami warnings were issued, cancelled, or what coastal authorities should do now.
Prioritization exists but is implicit; the report does not explicitly rank which region is highest priority for resource pre-positioning versus lower-priority watch.
No guidance on which jurisdictions or partner agencies (e.g., Pacific Tsunami Warning Center, Indonesian BMKG, Chilean SHOA) should be contacted or queried for updates.
